title: Health Sciences Authority (Amendment) and Other Matters Bill
what_it_is: Health Sciences Authority (Amendment) and Other Matters Bill

sections.label: Health Information Act and psychologist registration
sections.summary: The Health Information Act was enacted this year, and statutory registration of psychologists is now being planned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, we enacted the Health Information Act to govern and safeguard key health information, including in the National Electronic Health Record.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We are now planning for the statutory registration of psychologists, including clinical psychologists and educational psychologists, to promote higher care standards and support better care outcomes.

sections.label: Community pharmacist influenza vaccination sandbox
sections.summary: MOH's Community Pharmacist Influenza Vaccination Sandbox showed positive results and is being considered for mainstreaming.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: MOH’s Community Pharmacist Influenza Vaccination Sandbox that was rolled out over the past year has shown positive results and we are looking at mainstreaming these services.

sections.label: Consolidating health regulatory functions under HSA
sections.summary: The Bill proposes consolidating health regulatory functions under HSA to protect patients and enable timely access to innovations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Bill therefore proposes to consolidate health regulatory functions and establish an integrated health regulatory function under HSA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This is not simply an organisational restructuring but an opportunity to lay the foundation for a more coherent, future-ready system that protects patients while enabling timely access to beneficial healthcare innovations, for patients’ benefit.

sections.label: HSA to administer HBRA and BATA
sections.summary: HSA will administer and regulate the Human Biomedical Research Act and the Biological Agents and Toxins Act, taking over from MOH.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: First, HSA will administer and regulate the Human Biomedical Research Act (HBRA) and the Biological Agents and Toxins Act (BATA), taking over these functions from MOH.

sections.label: Transfer of MOH and SPB functions to HSA
sections.summary: Existing approvals carry over, MOH functions transfer in November 2026 and SPB functions by end 2027, making HSA the integrated health regulator.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Existing approvals and permits will automatically be carried over, and regulated entities will not need to reapply or restart any processes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: First, MOH's regulatory functions and manpower will be transferred to HSA in November 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Thereafter, SPB's functions and manpower will be transferred to HSA by end 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: By bringing functions together, we can create broader career pathways, deepen regulatory expertise and strengthen HSA’s position as a trusted health regulator, building multidisciplinary regulatory capabilities for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Healthcare is being reshaped by AI, genomics and new care models, and our regulatory system must be capable of evolving around it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: By establishing HSA as Singapore’s integrated health regulator, we are building a system that is more coherent for the healthcare institutions, clearer for the healthcare professionals, more predictable for industry and ultimately, more responsive for patients.

sections.label: Future-ready regulatory system foundation
sections.summary: The Bill is a key milestone laying the foundation for a future-ready regulatory system trusted by the public and stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: It should provide clarity without unnecessary complexity and remain robust and agile to changes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This Bill is a key milestone, laying the foundation for a future-ready regulatory system trusted by the public and our stakeholders.

sections.label: Employee transfer and reskilling
sections.summary: MP asks for assurance that transferred employees will not be disadvantaged and asks what training will be provided as HSA becomes an integrated regulator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: First, can the Minister of State assure the House that employees affected by the transfer will not be disadvantaged in their remuneration, employment benefits and career progression?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Second, what training and reskilling opportunities will be provided, particularly where job scopes change as HSA becomes a more integrated regulator?

sections.label: No wrong door complaints
sections.summary: MP asks whether MOH can consider a "no wrong door" approach routing healthcare complaints to the appropriate regulatory body.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can MOH consider developing a "no wrong door" approach, where a consumer can raise a healthcare-related complaint and have it routed seamlessly to the appropriate regulatory body?

sections.label: Aggregating complaints and intelligence
sections.summary: MP asks whether HSA intends to aggregate complaints and regulatory intelligence and receive intelligence from frontline and consumer organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: An integrated regulator should be better positioned to connect these dots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore ask whether HSA intends to aggregate and analyse complaints and regulatory intelligence across its different functions and establish mechanisms to receive relevant intelligence from frontline organisations, including consumer organisations such as CASE, and the other professional bodies in the healthcare sector.

sections.label: Preserving Professional Boards independence
sections.summary: MP asks how the new arrangement will preserve the independence of Professional Boards and Councils while HSA takes on administrative support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Bill enables HSA to provide administrative support to the statutory bodies regulating healthcare professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how the new arrangement will preserve the independence of these Professional Boards and Councils, particularly in decisions relating to registration, professional standards and disciplinary matters, while HSA takes on a greater administrative and supporting role?

sections.label: Consolidation service standards outcomes
sections.summary: MP asks whether consolidation could lead to clearer service standards and more timely complaint and disciplinary processing, and hopes MOH and HSA track outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can the Minister of State therefore share whether this consolidation could lead to clearer service standards and more timely processing of complaints and disciplinary cases, while preserving the independence of the Professional Boards and fairness to all parties?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: After these changes are implemented, I hope both MOH and HSA will track tangible outcomes, such as licensing turnaround times, complaint resolution times and the timeliness of enforcement action.

sections.label: Quorum and board membership
sections.summary: Clause 5 sets quorum as the higher of three members or one-third of the Board, and clause 3 requires at least seven members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under clause 5 of this Bill, the quorum will become the higher of three members, or one-third of the authority's Board membership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Clause 3 will also replace the existing board membership range with a requirement that the authority must have at least seven members.

sections.label: HSA quorum falls to four
sections.summary: If HSA keeps its present composition, the quorum will fall from five members to four when clause 5 or new section 9 takes effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If HSA's composition remains at the present Chairperson plus 10 members, when clause 5 or the new section 9 kicks in after the Bill is passed today, the quorum will fall from five members to four.

sections.label: Biological Agents and Toxins Act transfer
sections.summary: The Bill transfers administration of the Biological Agents and Toxins Act from the Director-General of Health to HSA's Chief Executive and lets HSA assist with other health legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In 2003, a laboratory-acquired SARS infection highlighted the importance of strong national biosafety oversight, and contributed to the enactment of the Biological Agents and Toxins Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This Bill transfers responsibility for administering the Biological Agents and Toxins Act from the Director-General of Health to the Chief Executive of HSA through clauses 18 to 22, while clause 6 also empower HSA to assist in administering or enforcing a range of other health legislation listed in the new first schedule, including the Infectious Diseases Act.

sections.label: Temperature excursions disclosure timeline
sections.summary: MOH said temperature excursions from November 2020 were not disclosed during or after a September 2022 inspection and emerged after a July 2023 public complaint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: According to MOH's public statements temperature excursions stated back to November 2020 were not disclosed during or after a September 2022 routine inspection and the matter came to light only after a public complaint in July 2023.

sections.label: Officers inspect electronic material
sections.summary: Clause 26's proposed new section 45(2)(a) of the Human Biomedical Research Act permits authorised officers to inspect and copy electronic material.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under clause 26, the proposed new section 45(2)(a) of the Human Biomedical Research Act permits authorised officers to inspect and copy electronic material.

sections.label: Retention of information after investigations
sections.summary: The question asks what retention policies apply after investigations, given new section 45(12) lets an authorised officer keep information or things without payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: What retention policies will apply after investigations conclude particularly given that the proposed new section 45(12) entitles an authorised officer without payment to keep information or things or copies or extracts provided under section 45(9)(a)?

sections.label: Appointment of auxiliary authorised officers
sections.summary: The Bill allows appointment of auxiliary authorised officers, including suitably qualified private individuals, under clauses 24 and 34.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Bill allows the appointment of the auxiliary authorised officers, including suitably qualified private individuals under clauses 24 and 34 of the Bill respectively.

sections.label: HSA role in statutory decisions
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to confirm HSA's role is confined to administrative services, not statutory decision-making on registration, standards, complaints, investigations or discipline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister confirm that HSA's role will be confined to administrative services and will not extend to statutory decision-making concerning registration, professional standards, complaints, investigations or discipline?

sections.label: Reduced quorum for HSA Board
sections.summary: Under the new provisions, a meeting may be held with four members, fewer than the current quorum of five, while HSA's powers and functions expand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under the new provisions, a meeting may be held with only four members present, fewer than the current quorum of five.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: HSA's powers and functions are expanding, yet the minimum quorum for Board meetings is being reduced.

sections.label: Safeguarding regulatory bodies' independence
sections.summary: HSA will provide administrative support to healthcare professional regulatory bodies, but their independent functions in registration, discipline and professional standards must be safeguarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Although HSA will provide administrative support to the healthcare professional regulatory bodies, their independent functions in registration, disciplinary matters and professional standards must continue to be safeguarded.

sections.label: Cordlife cord-blood units investigation
sections.summary: About 17,050 Cordlife clients had cord-blood units in six tanks under investigation; audits found further lapses and MOH stopped new cord-blood collection and processing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Approximately 17,050 Cordlife clients had cord-blood units in six tanks that came under investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Subsequent audits identified further governance, incident-reporting and operational lapses, and MOH stopped new cord-blood collection and processing.

sections.label: Transfer of MOH divisions to HSA
sections.summary: The Bill transfers MOH's Regulatory Compliance, Regulatory Transformation and Surveillance and Enforcement Divisions to HSA, expanding its responsibilities across healthcare services, biomedical research and biological agents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill transfers MOH’s Regulatory Compliance, Regulatory Transformation and Surveillance and Enforcement Divisions to HSA, expanding its responsibilities across healthcare services, biomedical research and biological agents.

sections.label: Auxiliary authorised officers' limited powers
sections.summary: The Bill allows suitably qualified persons outside the Public Service to become auxiliary authorised officers, who cannot search premises, inspect medical records, seize items, or test and remove samples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill allows suitably qualified persons outside the Public Service to become auxiliary authorised officers under the Human Biomedical Research Act and Healthcare Services Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This may increase inspection capacity, but unlike full officers, they cannot search premises, inspect medical records, seize items, or test and remove biological samples and specified materials.

sections.label: Consent and entry provisions
sections.summary: Asks whether the Minister will amend provisions to state that entry requires consent and refusing consent is not an offence or obstruction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Minister amend the provisions to state expressly that entry requires consent and that refusing consent is neither an offence nor an act of obstruction?

sections.label: HSA enforcement code of conduct
sections.summary: Asks whether HSA will publish a clear enforcement code of conduct before auxiliary officers begin work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will HSA publish a clear enforcement code of conduct before auxiliary officers begin work?

sections.label: HSA workforce and capacity plan
sections.summary: Asks whether HSA will publish a workforce and capacity plan showing how critical gaps will be filled without weakening product-safety responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will HSA publish a workforce and capacity plan showing how critical gaps will be filled without weakening existing product-safety responsibilities?

sections.label: HSA first-year transition audit
sections.summary: Asks whether HSA will publish a first-year transition audit and dashboard covering turnaround times, inspection coverage, incident responses, complaints and smaller-provider burdens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will HSA publish a first-year transition audit and dashboard covering turnaround times, risk-based inspection coverage, serious-incident responses, auxiliary-officer complaints and smaller-provider compliance burdens?

sections.label: Reliable evidence and US marketing
sections.summary: States that because she insisted on reliable evidence, it was never commercially marketed in the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Because she insisted on reliable evidence, it was never commercially marketed in the US.

sections.label: HSA judgement and trust
sections.summary: States that where evidence is strong delay can harm, and that HSA must exercise judgement, with the Bill strengthening an invisible contract of trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Where evidence is strong, delay can harm too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: That is the deeper responsibility we place on HSA: not merely to move quickly or cautiously, but to exercise the judgement to know what the evidence demands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A regulator's greatest successes are often quiet: (a) the vape that never reaches a child's schoolbag; (b) the data breach that never compromises a patient; (c) the dangerous practice corrected before someone is harmed; (d) the cord blood unit still viable when a family finally needs it; and (e) the breakthrough therapy that reaches a patient in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If this Bill gives HSA the reach to act, the restraint to remain trusted and the readiness to prevent harm while enabling timely access to beneficial innovation, it will strengthen that invisible contract of trust.

sections.label: HSA regulatory role transfer
sections.summary: The Bill transfers regulatory weight to HSA, with MOH as policy maker and HSA as regulator.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Bill transfers real regulatory weight to HSA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It draws a sharper line, MOH as the policy maker and HSA as the regulator.

sections.label: Auxiliary authorised officers powers
sections.summary: The Bill lets HSA's chief executive appoint auxiliary authorised officers who may enter and inspect premises with consent during normal business hours.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Bill lets HSA's chief executive appoint auxiliary authorised officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Under the Healthcare Services Act, they may enter and inspect premises with consent during normal business hours.

sections.label: Clause 36C assurance extension
sections.summary: Clause 36C extends the same assurance to a new generation of officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, clause 36C of this Bill extends the same assurance to a new generation of officers.

sections.label: Transferring employee employment terms
sections.summary: On the transfer date, every transferring employee moves to the authority on terms no less favourable than before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Understandably, some may ask what this re-organisation will mean for their jobs, their employment terms and also their future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It provides that, on the transfer date, every transferring employee moves to the service of the authority, and I quote: “on terms no less favourable than those enjoyed by the employee on the eve of the first transfer date." This is an important assurance.

sections.label: Preservation of employment terms
sections.summary: Clause 36D provides for the general preservation of employment terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is the right principle and I am heartened to see that it is stated plainly in the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also welcome clause 36D, which provides for the general preservation of the employment terms.

sections.label: HSA terms with AUSBE
sections.summary: The speaker hopes HSA will work with AUSBE on comprehensive, fair and equitable terms for transferred officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is a fair and necessary transitional safeguard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But it also points to an important next step, and here I would like to highlight to HSA that as it develops the new terms and conditions that will apply to the transferred officers, I hope that it will take into consideration, work strongly with AUSBE, so that they make sure they can come up with a comprehensive, fair and equitable sets of terms and conditions for the officers that are transferred.

sections.label: HSA healthcare regulatory consolidation
sections.summary: The Bill consolidates healthcare regulatory functions within HSA, expanding its remit to facility regulation, research oversight, biological agent control and board support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to consolidate important healthcare regulatory functions within HSA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will expand HSA’s current remit from primarily product regulation, for example, relating to health products, devices, blood and forensic science, to encompass facility regulation, biomedical research oversight, biological agent control and administrative support for the professional boards.

sections.label: Two-stage transition implementation
sections.summary: The Minister of State indicated the transition will be implemented in two stages, in November 2026 and next year for SPB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Minister of State has indicated that the implementation of this transition will be in two stages – November 2026 and, I believe for SPB, it will be next year.

sections.label: Old complaint cases uncleared
sections.summary: Old complaint cases lodged well before 2020 have yet to be cleared.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As of now, there are still old complaint cases that were lodged well before 2020 that have yet to be cleared.

sections.label: Biological agents powers transfer
sections.summary: The Bill transfers substantial powers under the Biological Agents and Toxins Act from the Director-General of Health to HSA's Chief Executive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill transfers substantial powers under the Biological Agents and Toxins Act from the Director-General of Health (DGH) to HSA's Chief Executive (CE).

sections.label: Consultation as mandatory pre-requisite
sections.summary: The question asks whether the consultation process is intended to be a mandatory procedural pre-requisite to lawful exercise of power.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is this consultation process intended to be a mandatory procedural pre-requisite to the lawful exercise of power?

sections.label: Consequence of non-compliance
sections.summary: The question asks what the consequence of non-compliance is if consultation is mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If consultation is mandatory, what is the consequence of non-compliance?

sections.label: Resourcing expanded mandate question
sections.summary: The Minister of State is asked to clarify how the expanded mandate will be resourced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister of State clarify how the expanded mandate will be resourced?

sections.label: Support for Bill and sitting suspended
sections.summary: Subject to assurances, the speaker supports the Bill and suspends the Sitting until 3.45 pm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Subject to these assurances, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have been in the Chambers for five hours now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.45 pm.

sections.label: Consolidating work into HSA secretariat
sections.summary: The Bill consolidates this work into one secretariat within HSA, an agency already running regulatory operations at scale.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill's answer is to consolidate this work into one secretariat within HSA, an agency that already runs regulatory operations at scale.

sections.label: Governance protocol and timeliness standards
sections.summary: The speaker asks that inspection and complaint functions be separated in a published governance protocol with independent review, and that timeliness standards be published.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, that the separation of the authority's inspection and complaint functions from its secretariat function be set out in a published governance protocol, and that the arrangement be subject to periodic independent review.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, that the Ministry publish timeliness standards for the new secretariat, in particular, the median time from complaint to Complaints Committee decision, reported regularly, and commit to keeping both parties, complainant and professional, informed of the progress of their case and directed to available support throughout.

sections.label: Detection capability and medical records line
sections.summary: The authority should build capability to detect fabricated and AI-generated research data, distinguish routine assurance from for-cause investigation, and hold the line on medical records.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The authority should build the capability to detect fabricated and AI-generated research data from the outset of its stewardship, not after the first serious case arises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Inspection practice should distinguish clearly between routine assurance and for-cause investigation, so that a visit that finds nothing costs nothing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also note the firm line the Bill draws around medical records for the new auxiliary officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That line protects patient confidentiality, and it must hold in practice as it reads in law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A professional who fears the disciplinary system practises defensively: more tests, more referrals, less candour when things go wrong.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A professional who trusts it discloses error earlier, and patients are safer for it.

sections.label: Consolidating regulatory functions under HSA
sections.summary: The Bill consolidates regulatory functions from the Ministry, the Human Biomedical Research Act, and the Secretariat of Healthcare Professional Boards under HSA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The provisions in this Bill are not abstract to me.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill consolidates regulatory functions from the Ministry, the Human Biomedical Research Act, and the Secretariat of Healthcare Professional Boards under HSA.

sections.label: HSA classification turnaround time
sections.summary: The passage asks whether HSA will commit to a defined turnaround time for classification decisions on genuinely novel products.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share whether HSA intends to commit to a defined turnaround time for classification decisions on genuinely novel products, so that predictability becomes something innovators can plan around and not just a description of intent?

sections.label: Advisory panels and IRB standards
sections.summary: The passage asks whether technical advisory panels' composition and expertise will be disclosed to Parliament and whether IRB training standards will be harmonised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I accept it would be impractical to legislate rigid criteria for scientific advisory input, since the expertise needed will keep evolving.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But could the Minister confirm whether, once technical advisory panels for domains like human biomedical research and AI-enabled devices are formed, their composition and areas of expertise will be disclosed to Parliament, even if only after the fact?

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is a well-recognised feature of research governance in Singapore and internationally that IRB rigour and panel composition can vary between institutions, and that reviewers are not always specialists in the particular research area before them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would ask whether this restructuring includes any parallel effort to harmonise IRB training or competency standards across institutions.

sections.label: Healthcare regulatory operations in HSA
sections.summary: The passage states the move will house healthcare regulatory operations across products, services, health information and professionals within HSA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As I shared earlier, this move will house healthcare regulatory operations across products, services, health information and professionals within a single organisation, HSA.

sections.label: MOH leads public health response
sections.summary: The passage states MOH will continue to lead the overall public health response and national decision-making, including under the Infectious Diseases Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: MOH will continue to lead the overall public health response and national decision-making, including under the Infectious Diseases Act.

sections.label: Revised quorum threshold and board size
sections.summary: The passage states the revised quorum threshold and expects HSA's board size to grow beyond its current 11 members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The revised quorum threshold, set at the higher of one-third of Board members or a minimum of three members, is aligned with other Statutory Boards, such as the Energy Market Authority, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore and the Communicable Diseases Agency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: More importantly, this amendment should be considered in the broader context of the changes to HSA's board governance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We expect the board size to grow beyond its current 11 members to meet HSA’s expanded mandate.

sections.label: Transfer of manpower and resources
sections.summary: The passage states manpower and resources, including legal, IT and corporate support, will be transferred from MOH and SMC to HSA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: With the transfer of functions, the corresponding manpower and resources, including legal, information technology and corporate support within MOH and SMC will be transferred to HSA.

sections.label: AAO powers and entry
sections.summary: AAOs cannot exercise the full range of authorised officer powers, and their entry under these provisions is consent-based.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: AAOs cannot exercise the full range of powers available to authorised officers under the relevant legislation, including search, seizure and other investigative powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: On the issue of entry raised by Mr Yip and Dr Hamid, the policy intent is that entry by AAOs under these provisions is consent-based as routine inspections and audits, where AAOs are likely to be deployed, are generally pre-arranged and scheduled in advance.

sections.label: HSA data governance requirements
sections.summary: HSA will abide by prevailing public sector data governance requirements, including data storage, disposal and sharing with third parties such as AAOs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As a Statutory Board, HSA will continue to abide by prevailing public sector data governance requirements, including how HSA manages information, such as data storage, data disposal and sharing with third parties, such as AAOs.

sections.label: SPB functions under HSA
sections.summary: Moving SPB's functions to HSA strengthens administrative capability and case management consistency, without affecting the Professional Boards' and Councils' independence and statutory autonomy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Bringing the functions of SPB under HSA will strengthen the administrative capability and consistency of case management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: However, the transfer of functions does not affect the independence and statutory autonomy of the Professional Boards and Councils over healthcare professional matters, for instance, over professional standards and disciplinary decisions.

sections.label: Phased SPB move to HSA
sections.summary: SPB will be moved to HSA at a later stage, allowing a phased approach to reviewing operational arrangements and setting out governance measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For this reason, SPB will be moved to HSA at a later stage, allowing a phased and careful approach to reviewing and finetuning these operational arrangements, including setting out clear governance measures.

sections.label: Strengthening case management communication
sections.summary: Complainants and professionals are kept informed at various inquiry stages, and case management will be strengthened to provide clearer communication and appropriate support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Today, complainants and professionals are kept informed of outcomes at various stages of the inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will look into strengthening the case management process to provide clearer communication to both complainants and professionals throughout the process and ensure that appropriate support is available to them.

sections.label: Reskilling for job scope changes
sections.summary: Where job scope changes, officers will receive reskilling opportunities and on-the-job training to equip them for evolving responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Where job scope changes, officers will be provided with reskilling opportunities and on-the-job training so that officers are equipped with the capabilities needed for their evolving responsibilities.

sections.label: HSA advice on AI devices
sections.summary: HSA will advise on governance structures for safe AI device deployment, regulatory sandboxes, and work with Professional Boards and Councils on safe and ethical AI use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: HSA will also be better placed to advise on the governance structures needed to ensure the safe deployment of such AI devices within institutions, including the rollout of regulatory sandboxes where appropriate, and to work with the Professional Boards and Councils on the safe and ethical use of AI devices by healthcare professionals in day-to-day practice.

sections.label: No performance indicators yet
sections.summary: The immediate focus is smooth transition and operational continuity, so prescribing specific performance indicators now is premature pending further work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Our immediate focus is on ensuring a smooth transition and operational continuity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: It is therefore premature to prescribe specific performance indicators at this point as further work is needed to ensure that any adopted indicators truly reflect and drive the organisation towards the outcomes we have described.

sections.label: Phased implementation for continuity
sections.summary: Engagement continues so stakeholders know who to approach for regulatory matters, and phased implementation allows stabilising phase one and preparing phase two without disruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will continue to engage them and ensure that they know who to approach for their respective regulatory matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This is also why implementation is phased, allowing us to stabilise the first phase, learning from implementation, and prepare for the second phase so as to ensure that regulatory services and ongoing cases continue without disruption throughout the transition.

sections.label: Timely risk-based regulation
sections.summary: The objective is timely, evidence-based, risk-proportionate regulation, with HSA timelines comparable to overseas counterparts and resources directed to greatest potential harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The objective is therefore not regulation that is invariably faster, but regulation that is timely, evidence-based and proportionate to risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: It is also worth noting that HSA's regulatory timelines are comparable with those of other established overseas regulatory counterparts, particularly for innovative medicines and medical devices, reflecting a careful balance between efficiency and rigorous assessment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: A risk-based approach directs regulatory attention and resources to where the potential harm is greatest and regulatory requirements, inspections, and enforcement should be calibrated accordingly while maintaining the standards necessary to protect patients.

sections.label: Integrated healthcare regulatory system
sections.summary: HSA in its expanded scope will ensure regulatory interfaces work coherently so research is protected, innovation progresses, and emerging risks are addressed collectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Nonetheless, HSA in its expanded scope will continue to ensure that the regulatory interfaces work coherently with the relevant institutions and agencies so that good research is protected, beneficial innovation can progress responsibly towards patients and emerging risks are addressed collectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I will say that this Bill is about building a more integrated, responsive and future-ready healthcare regulatory system to meet emerging challenges.
